Plots brma Object

Source: R/plot-main.R
plot.brma.Rd

plot.brma visualizes posterior (and prior) distribution a brma object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
plot(
  x,
  parameter,
  parameter_mods,
  parameter_scale,
  prior = FALSE,
  standardized_coefficients = FALSE,
  conditional = FALSE,
  output_measure = NULL,
  transform = NULL,
  plot_type = "base",
  dots_prior = NULL,
  density_method = c("KDE", "qCMDE", "IWMDE"),
  density_control = NULL,
  component = "auto",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
lines(
  x,
  parameter = NULL,
  parameter_mods = NULL,
  parameter_scale = NULL,
  prior = FALSE,
  standardized_coefficients = FALSE,
  conditional = FALSE,
  output_measure = NULL,
  transform = NULL,
  plot_type = "base",
  dots_prior = NULL,
  density_method = c("KDE", "qCMDE", "IWMDE"),
  density_control = NULL,
  component = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a fitted brma, BMA, or RoBMA object.

parameter

a parameter to be plotted. Defaults to "mu" for the effect size, or to the meta-regression intercept when moderators are present. Additional options are "tau", "rho" for multilevel models, "PET", "PEESE", and "omega" or "weightfunction" for selection models. Use plot_pet_peese() for PET/PEESE regression plots. Factor terms select all coefficient cells; use a semantic selector such as "group[level]" to plot one cell. Structural point masses are retained. A quantity of the fitted model that is no model parameter (an inclusion indicator such as "mu_x_indicator", "bias_indicator", a weight-function coordinate such as "omega[1]", or a latent cluster effect) stops with the classes BayesTools_hypothesis_target and BayesTools_hypothesis_unavailable, with which hypothesis() refuses it. Ordered level cells retain their semantic marginal draws and prior metadata on the requested predictor scale, including conditional row alignment.

parameter_mods

legacy moderator selector. Prefer parameter with component = "mods". Use "intercept" for the adjusted effect in meta-regression models.

parameter_scale

legacy scale-regression selector. Prefer parameter with component = "scale". Use "intercept" for the heterogeneity intercept in location-scale models.

prior

whether prior distribution should be added to figure. Defaults to FALSE.

standardized_coefficients

whether to plot moderator and scale-regression coefficients on the standardized predictor scale. Defaults to FALSE.

conditional

whether to plot the conditional posterior distribution for RoBMA product-space objects. Defaults to FALSE.

output_measure

effect-size measure for location/effect predictions. Defaults to the fitted measure. Supported conversions are among "SMD", "COR", "ZCOR", and "OR"; "RR", "HR", "IRR", "RD", and "GEN" can only be returned on their fitted measure. Use transform = "EXP" for ratio-scale output from log-scale measures.

transform

optional plotting transformation. "EXP" exponentiates effect-size location and individual meta-regression coefficients for fitted log-scale OR, RR, HR, and IRR models. For scale-regression coefficients, "EXP" displays the multiplicative change in heterogeneity. "LOG" displays a positive heterogeneity intercept or random-effect variance or SD multiplier on the log scale. The transformation is applied to KDE and precomputed qCMDE/IWMDE densities with the corresponding Jacobian. For automatically unscaled scale-formula intercepts, use standardized_coefficients = TRUE with qCMDE/IWMDE.

plot_type

whether to use a base plot "base" or ggplot2 "ggplot" for plotting. Defaults to "base".

dots_prior

list of additional graphical arguments to be passed to the plotting function of the prior distribution. Supported arguments are lwd, lty, col, and col.fill, to adjust the line thickness, line type, line color, and fill color of the prior distribution respectively. For ordered predictor targets, omitted line colors and types match each posterior level's color with a dashed prior curve, including selected cells. For selected ordered cells with prior = TRUE, color/colour aliases resolve to col, with priority col, color, then colour; linetype takes precedence over lty in both renderers. Explicit col, lty, or linetype values take precedence; the ordinary prior defaults are retained for other targets. Ordered metadata validation is restricted to the selected terms, including selected group members; unrelated ordered terms do not affect prior styles.

density_method

posterior density method. "KDE" uses the standard BayesTools kernel density estimate. "qCMDE" attaches RoBMA row-normalized q-grid conditional densities. "IWMDE" attaches Chen-style moment-matched IWMDE densities. qCMDE is preferred when its additional normalization cost is acceptable; IWMDE can be faster but is more sensitive to its fitted conditional weights. Matching is case-insensitive. Ordered effects use the same normalized conditional-source estimator for both methods, with their respective posterior-row budgets. Selected weightfunction models near zero cumulative ordered effects can take more than 10 minutes with qCMDE or IWMDE. Exact regular ordered offsets that need a finite supplier integral use a positive conditional block; offsets classified as nonfinite or unsupported are omitted only at that exact value from a density curve. Point hypotheses retain their structural or precision refusal. For semantic random-effect quantities, qCMDE/IWMDE support direct scalar fitted sources, allocated component SDs backed by a scalar aggregate (tau_total or tau_common), and allocation proportions or multipliers backed by a fitted simplex coordinate. Other nonlinear derived quantities remain KDE-only. Shared inclusion gates are supported for aggregate and component SDs and allocation proportions. SDs retain their excluded zero branches; proportions condition on positive total heterogeneity. Allocated component SDs in a predictor-scaled block require standardized_coefficients = TRUE or density_method = 'KDE' for an original-scale request. This block-wide limitation also covers a centered intercept whose value happens to be unchanged by scaling. A positive point source multiplied by stochastic allocation weights has a continuous target law, but its source-held-weight chart cannot sweep that target; use density_method = 'KDE'. Source-zero and inclusion-gate atoms retain their declared locations. In independently gated allocations, realized tau_total/tau2_total and tau2_prop(...) are KDE-only because they combine multiple gate and allocation coordinates. Their structural point masses are displayed separately from the continuous density; tau2_prop(...) is conditioned on positive realized total heterogeneity. qCMDE/IWMDE are not available for non-known-V brma.mv() random-formula models, brma.mv() models with component-specific scale formulas (a named scale list), or selection-weightfunction coordinates requiring joint replacement. IWMDE is also unavailable for binomial and Poisson GLMMs; use qCMDE for GLMM density plots. qCMDE/IWMDE densities are evaluated on the fitted coefficient coordinate. If automatic predictor scaling changes the requested display coordinate, use standardized_coefficients = TRUE; RoBMA does not infer a coefficient transformation from posterior draws.

density_control

named list of density-estimation settings. Supported entries are n_points (default 100), samples (default 500 for qCMDE and 1000 for IWMDE density curves), target_relative_mcse (default 0.05), display_grid (default "adaptive"), normalization_points (default NULL, resolved to max(50, n_points)), and normalization_prob (default 0.999; see hypothesis() for the per-row truncation it permits). integration_control (default NULL) retains the fitted selection-integration settings. Supply a control created by set_selection_likelihood_control() to change those settings for this post-fit calculation, for example list(integration_control = set_selection_likelihood_control(max_points_per_scramble = 32768)). This entry is available for Gaussian selection models with a fitted integration plan. The fitted object and posterior draws are unchanged. The maximum point budget controls factor QMC fallback; analytic and deterministic quadrature rules remain unchanged. samples controls the fixed posterior-row budget for the density curve. target_relative_mcse is a point-ordinate diagnostic target and does not alter this fixed-budget density plot. The normalization entries are used with density_method = "qCMDE" and density_method = "IWMDE". Curve diagnostics apply local relative-MCSE, effective-sample-size, and contribution-concentration gates over the empirical 5–95 percent bulk and record the 5 and 95 percent tail checkpoints. The entire display retains an absolute MCSE safeguard relative to the density peak. Requested point ordinates used for Bayes factors retain separate strict local diagnostics. Increase the row and normalization budgets and compare results when density diagnostics report low effective sample size, concentrated contributions, or unstable normalization.

component

parameter component. Defaults to "auto", which infers the component when possible. Use "mods" (alias "location"), "scale", "random", or "bias" to disambiguate terms used in multiple model components. The random component selects semantic standard deviation, correlation, and allocation parameters from brma.mv() random formulas. A parameter_mods or parameter_scale selection with another component stops with an error of class RoBMA_component_mismatch.

...

list of additional graphical arguments to be passed to the plotting function. Supported arguments are lwd, lty, col, col.fill, xlab, ylab, ylab2, main, xlim, ylim, and ylim2 to adjust the line thickness, line type, line color, fill color, x-label, density-axis label, probability-axis label, title, x-axis range, density-axis range, and probability-axis range respectively. Set ylim2 on the initial plot() call; subsequent base lines() calls reuse that probability mapping.

Value

plot.brma returns either NULL if plot_type = "base" or a ggplot2 object (a named list of plots for a whole factor term) if plot_type = "ggplot". lines.brma returns NULL for plot_type = "base" and ggplot2 layer(s) for plot_type = "ggplot".

Details

A qCMDE/IWMDE request that the fitted model does not support stops before any density is estimated with an error of class RoBMA_density_method_unavailable and one class naming the cause: RoBMA_density_method_random_unknown_v (brma.mv() random-formula models without known V), RoBMA_density_method_scale_components (component-specific scale formulas), or RoBMA_density_method_glmm (IWMDE for binomial and Poisson GLMMs). Requests that are unavailable for the plotted quantity stop with the same parent class and RoBMA_density_method_conditional_random (conditional random-effect plots, which are KDE-only), RoBMA_density_method_random_target (a random-effect quantity without a supported scalar random-component coordinate), RoBMA_density_method_bias_target (a composite weightfunction target; use density_method = 'KDE'), or RoBMA_density_method_original_scale (a coefficient or factor cell whose original-scale value is not a linear combination of its fitted coefficients, such as the exponentiated intercept of a scale formula with standardized predictors; use standardized_coefficients = TRUE). A density whose construction fails stops with an error of class RoBMA_density_construction_error (a RoBMA_density_error); use density_method = "KDE" to estimate it from the posterior draws. A fitted chain with no eligible row of the target adds the class RoBMA_density_chain_coverage, and the message names longer chains and their convergence as the other remedy. hypothesis() refuses qCMDE/IWMDE for the same causes with these classes after its own. plot_prior() stops with RoBMA_density_method_original_scale for the prior of a term with several fitted coordinates whose original-scale coordinates the standardization changes (see there).

A returned qCMDE/IWMDE estimate that fails the density availability checks raises a RoBMA_density_plot_error identifying the plotted parameter. Its density_diagnostics field contains the returned diagnostic records, including computed density values and selected rows, without executable estimate plans that could retain the fitted object.

lines.brma() adds the posterior density to an existing base plot. Omit add: this method always adds, and supplying add triggers an error. With plot_type = "ggplot", it returns ggplot2 layer(s) that can be added to a plot.brma(..., plot_type = "ggplot") object with +. For base plots containing point masses, the initial plot.brma() call establishes the secondary probability axis and lines.brma() reuses it across fitted objects. An overlaid point mass outside the initial ylim2 is clipped with a warning.

See also

RoBMA()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.lehmann2018, package = "metadat")
  fit <- bPET(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = dat.lehmann2018, measure = "SMD")

  plot(fit, parameter = "mu")
  lines(fit, parameter = "mu", col = "blue", lwd = 2)

  ggplot_fit <- plot(fit, parameter = "mu", plot_type = "ggplot")
  ggplot_fit + lines(fit, parameter = "mu", plot_type = "ggplot", col = "blue")

  plot(fit, parameter = "tau", prior = TRUE)
  plot(fit, parameter = "PET")
}
} # }
